description: Feature backlog - Product Owner owns priority

items.title: Enrich retry failure context with structured ac_results references
items.intent: Developer retry attempts must receive precise file:line failure references from prior attempts so they fix the right code — attempt 1 context must survive to attempt 3 even under truncation
steps: In _capture_retry_failure() around line 2577, after capturing diff_summary, check if STATUS_DIR/result.json exists and extract ac_results using jq. For each failed AC (met==false), format a compact line like 'AC{index} FAIL: {issue} ({file}:{line})'. Append these compact failure lines to the entry variable
In _build_prior_failure_context() around line 2600, increase max_body_chars from 2000 to 4000

Change the truncation logic in _build_prior_failure_context(): when an entry would exceed the cap, instead of dropping it entirely with the text 'earlier attempts truncated', extract the compact AC failure lines from the dropped entry and prepend them as a condensed summary. Remove or replace the literal string 'earlier attempts truncated' with something that preserves the failure references

acceptanceCriteria.text: max_body_chars in _build_prior_failure_context is 4000 or greater
When result.json contains ac_results with failed ACs, _capture_retry_failure includes file:line references in the entry
Truncated entries preserve compact failure summaries instead of being dropped entirely

items.title: Deduplicate AC verify execution — validator trusts orchestrator results
items.intent: AC verify commands must not run three times per sprint — the validator must be explicitly told to trust orchestrator results and redirect its effort to intent fulfillment and integration correctness instead of re-running commands
steps: In _run_validation_cycle() where validator_extra is built with ac_report (around lines 2476-2479), change the injection to include an explicit instruction telling the validator to trust the provided AC verification results and NOT re-run AC verify commands. Redirect the validator to focus on: (1) whether the implementation fulfills the item intent beyond mechanical AC pass, (2) integration correctness — is new code wired into the codebase and reachable, (3) ACs without verify commands that need manual probing
Make the trust-results instruction conditional — only inject it when ac_report is non-empty

Also update line 1687 in build_agent_prompt() where it currently says 'run every one of them' for AC verify commands — this contradicts the new trust instruction. Change it to say the orchestrator runs AC verify commands authoritatively and results will be provided, so the validator should review results rather than re-run

acceptanceCriteria.text: validator_extra includes instruction to trust orchestrator AC results and not re-run them
acceptanceCriteria.verify: grep -q 'Trust these results\|trust these results\|Trust the results\|trust the results' .aishore/aishore

acceptanceCriteria.text: The instruction redirects validator focus to intent fulfillment and integration
Line 1687 no longer tells validator to run every AC verify command
acceptanceCriteria.verify: ! grep -q 'run every one of them.*primary evidence' .aishore/aishore

items.title: Inject integration enforcement rules into validator context
items.intent: When an item has AC verify commands testing reachability, the validator must treat disconnected or unreachable code as a hard failure — not an advisory note — closing the loophole where code passes ACs mechanically but is never called from real entry points
steps: In _run_validation_cycle(), after building validator_extra with AC results and the trust-results instruction, add an Integration Enforcement section to validator_extra

Read the sprint.json acceptanceCriteria to determine whether any AC has verify commands. If yes: inject text saying disconnected code (new functions, modules, or routes not reachable from any existing entry point) is a validation failure, not advisory. If no verify commands exist (scaffolding/infrastructure items): inject text saying integration issues remain advisory notes only
The enforcement text must go into validator_extra (runtime injection), NOT into .aishore/agents/validator.md

acceptanceCriteria.text: Validator_extra includes an Integration Enforcement section
Integration enforcement treats disconnected code as failure when verify commands exist
Integration enforcement distinguishes items with verify commands from items without
The validator agent prompt file is not modified

items.title: Enforce maturity protocol phases in developer result.json
items.intent: Developer agents must prove they completed Critique and Harden phases with structured evidence in result.json — skipping phases must cause the orchestrator to reject the submission as incomplete
steps: In the maturity protocol injection text (around line 1659-1663), append a structured output requirement explaining that result.json must include a '"phases"' object (use the literal JSON key) with critique (containing findings_count) and harden (containing verify_commands_run and verify_commands_passed). State clearly that the orchestrator will reject results missing this field

Modify check_result() (lines 1832-1864) to accept an optional first argument for agent role (e.g. 'developer' or 'validator'). When role is 'developer' and status is 'pass', use jq to check for .phases in result.json. If phases is missing, null, or empty, log an error about missing maturity evidence and return 1
In _run_developer_cycle() at the check_result call (around line 2415), pass 'developer' as the first argument
In _run_validation_cycle() at the check_result call (around line 2481), pass 'validator' as the first argument so phase enforcement is not applied to validators

acceptanceCriteria.text: check_result accepts a role parameter and enforces phases for developer role
check_result passes validator results without phase enforcement
Maturity protocol injection tells developer to include a phases JSON key in result.json
check_result function contains logic to verify the phases field

items.title: Enforce mandatory ac_results in validator result.json
items.intent: Every validator failure must include structured per-AC results so retry context is always precise and targeted — generic failure text alone is not acceptable as validator output
steps: In _run_validation_cycle() around line 2476, before calling run_agent validator, append a section to validator_extra that requires the validator to include an ac_results array in result.json. The text must contain 'ac_results' and explain the required structure: array of objects with ac_index (int), met (bool), and either summary (if met) or issue/file/line (if not met). Use the phrase 'MUST include' or 'must include' to make the requirement clear

After the check_result call on the validator result (around line 2481), when result is fail, use jq to check for .ac_results in result.json. If missing or null, call log_warning with a message containing the word 'degraded' about reduced retry precision

acceptanceCriteria.text: validator_extra injection contains ac_results requirement with MUST/must include
A log_warning with the word degraded is emitted when ac_results is missing from a failed validator result
The injected text describes ac_index, met, and issue fields as part of the required structure

items.title: Add regression suite clean and skip support
items.intent: Operators must be able to clear a flaky regression suite with backup and skip specific entries by item ID — flaky or obsolete regressions must never permanently block all future sprints with no escape hatch
steps: In .aishore/lib/cmd-clean.sh cmd_clean(), add --regression flag support via parse_opts. When --regression and --dry-run: count lines in ARCHIVE_DIR/regression.jsonl, report count. When --regression without --dry-run: create a backup copy of regression.jsonl (with .bak extension), then remove the original. Print confirmation with entry count and backup path

In .aishore/aishore _run_regression_suite(), before the execution loop, check for ARCHIVE_DIR/regression-skip.json. If it exists and is valid JSON, read it as an array of item IDs to skip. Inside the loop, compare each entry itemId against the skip list and continue (skip execution) if matched. Log the count of skipped entries after the loop

acceptanceCriteria.text: Help text for clean command documents the --regression flag
cmd-clean.sh contains regression handling code that creates a backup file
regression-skip.json support exists in the orchestrator
